title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly derived and expressed as E = √3 mg / (3q).

title: Maximum speed tension
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be correctly derived and expressed as F = 2(√3 - 1)mg.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem correctly, equating the net work done by the electric and gravitational forces to the change in kinetic energy from A to B.

title: Force balance at max speed
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must identify that maximum speed occurs at the equilibrium position (where net tangential force is zero) and apply Newton's second law in the radial direction.

title: Trigonometric consistency
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the given angle (θ=60°) and related angles (e.g., 30°) in the expressions for work and force components.

title: Free-body diagram logic
description: Optional: The solution may include a clear free-body diagram or equivalent verbal description of the forces (tension, gravity, electric) acting on the ball.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assigning the sign (positive/negative work) for the gravitational or electric force when applying the work-energy theorem.

title: Equilibrium misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Mistaking the highest point B for the position of maximum speed, or incorrectly calculating the angle for the equilibrium position.
